stories.headline: Russian drone hits NATO member Romania; Tsahkna calls it proof Russia threatens all allies
stories.summary: A Russian drone launched against Ukraine strayed and struck an apartment building in Galați, Romania, injuring two people — the first NATO civilian casualties from a Russian strike. Estonian Foreign Minister Tsahkna responded prominently across international media, calling it proof that Russian aggression is not confined to Ukraine and citing Putin's 'increasing nervousness' over battlefield setbacks.

stories.headline: NATO assigns German-Netherlands Corps to command allied troops in Estonia and Latvia
stories.summary: NATO announced it will assign the German-Netherlands Corps, headquartered in Münster, as the tactical command headquarters for allied forces in Estonia and Latvia in the event of war with Russia, a transition expected to complete around mid-year 2026. The move is part of broader NATO eastern flank reinforcement as European allies assume more responsibility for their own defence.

stories.headline: Tsahkna at EU foreign ministers' Cyprus meeting: no talks with Russia now, more pressure needed
stories.summary: Estonian Foreign Minister Tsahkna was an active voice at the informal EU foreign ministers' summit in Limassol, Cyprus, warning that the EU would become a 'neutral mediator' if it rushed into direct Russia talks and arguing for 'strategic patience' and sustained pressure instead. He also described Ukraine's long-range strikes as 'long-range sanctions' that are working, and confirmed Estonia plans to continue military support at close to 3% of GDP in aid.

stories.headline: Kevadtorm 2026: Estonia's largest annual exercise tests allied cooperation and defence industry products
stories.summary: Estonia's largest annual military exercise, Kevadtorm (Spring Storm) 2026, involved active-duty troops, conscripts, reservists, Kaitseliit members, and allied units from France and the United Kingdom in joint artillery live-fire drills, and also served as a real-conditions testing platform for Estonian defence industry products including drone countermeasures and AI-enabled systems.

stories.headline: Reports of US reducing NATO military commitments prompt concern in Estonia
stories.summary: Reports, first published by Der Spiegel and subsequently picked up in Estonian media, indicated the US is planning to significantly reduce the military assets assigned to NATO in Europe — including strategic bombers and fighter jets — which was communicated to European allies at a closed briefing in Brussels. Estonian commentator Eerik-Niiles Kross described the potential cuts as 'genuinely dangerous,' while Estonian-language outlets covered the implications for the eastern flank.

stories.headline: Estonian government approves bill giving banks new powers to halt suspected fraud payments
stories.summary: Prime Minister Michal led a government press conference announcing approval of a bill that gives banks a legal basis to temporarily freeze payments suspected to involve fraud and to share fraud-related information with each other and with state agencies including the police and the Cyber Security Authority. The bill was presented against a backdrop of rising financial fraud losses, which reached approximately €29–31 million in 2025.

stories.headline: UK Defence Secretary Healey visits Tallinn to meet Pevkur; RAF jet GPS-jammed on return flight
stories.summary: UK Defence Secretary John Healey visited Tallinn to meet Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur for discussions on long-term bilateral defence cooperation. On the return journey, an RAF jet carrying Healey had its GPS navigation jammed for the entire three-hour flight, with smartphones and laptops also losing connectivity, in an incident attributed to Russian electronic warfare near the Russian border.

stories.headline: Pevkur urges Ukraine to tighten drone controls as Baltic airspace incursions raise political risks
stories.summary: Estonian Defence Minister Pevkur stated that Estonia has publicly urged Kyiv to tighten controls on drones to avoid political consequences among Western allies, while noting that Estonia has long prepared for potential Russian attacks. Separately, coverage addressed rising Baltic airspace incursions by Ukrainian drones targeting Russian Baltic ports, with Tsahkna and Latvian officials characterising Russian complaints as a sign of weakness.

stories.summary: Estonia's Transport Authority, in cooperation with Kaitseliit's West District pioneer unit, demolished the dilapidated Virtsu lighthouse using controlled explosives, accelerating a demolition that was already required for safety reasons while providing Kaitseliit members with additional training in demolishing tall structures.

stories.headline: Reform Party under political pressure as polls show continued slide; coalition scenarios debated
stories.summary: Multiple Estonian commentary pieces this week addressed the Reform Party's declining poll position (Norstat: 11%) and debated whether Prime Minister Michal would need to make a 'dramatic manoeuvre' to revive the party before elections. A Reform Party MP published an op-ed warning that an EKRE–Isamaa–Keskerakond coalition (dubbed 'EKREIKE 2.0') is not merely theoretical, while an SDE MP wrote critically that Reform has transformed into Isamaa's 'little brother.'

stories.headline: Pevkur tops Emor trust poll; remains most trusted government minister by wide margin
stories.summary: An Emor survey on trust in politicians showed Defence Minister Hanno Pevkur remains Estonia's most trusted minister with 28% of respondents, nearly ten percentage points ahead of the second-placed Social Affairs Minister Karmen Joller at 19%. Several newer cabinet members were largely unknown to respondents.

stories.headline: Estonian reservists' week launches; poll shows strong public support for 5% GDP defence spending
stories.summary: The Defence Ministry launched Reservists' Week (31 May – 7 June) honouring Estonia's approximately 100,000 reservists. A concurrent annual public opinion survey on national defence found that the vast majority of Estonian residents support maintaining or increasing the defence budget at the recently adopted minimum of 5% of GDP.

stories.headline: Women in Estonian defence highlighted in feature coverage and policy debate
stories.summary: Two separate pieces this week addressed the expanding role of women in Estonia's defence structures: an Eesti Naine profile of a Kaitseliit member and mother of two who sees defence participation as part of her identity, and an Õhtuleht opinion piece by former Prosecutor General Lavly Perling arguing that women's role in defence is not about replacing men but complementing them, as the defence resources authority openly advocates for women's military service inclusion.

stories.headline: Estonian tech startups seek collaboration with India at Latitude59 conference
stories.summary: Estonian startups in AI, cybersecurity, defence, and medicine are actively exploring partnerships with Indian companies, aiming to leverage India's large market. Media coverage noted President Alar Karis had visited India in February for an AI summit, and Latitude59 — a prominent Estonian startup conference — was serving as a platform for the outreach.

stories.headline: Two suspects arrested in fraud case targeting Estonian Artists' Union
stories.summary: Police arrested a 22-year-old Lithuanian national and a 21-year-old Estonian national in Maardu on 25 May, suspected of involvement in a fraud scheme targeting the Estonian Artists' Union. The scheme began on 7 May when a scammer posed as an Omniva postal worker to gain access to the Union's accountant. A court remanded both suspects in custody for two months.

stories.summary: Central-Eastern European banking group Erste Group initiated coverage of LHV Group shares with a buy recommendation and a 12-month price target of €4.40 per share, implying approximately 30% upside, in the first analyst report commissioned from the group.
